edit_summary: Allocate a gradient flexible-array object with room for one fewer copied stop.
root_cause: NSVGgradient embeds one stop and adds nstops - 1 extra slots before copying nstops parsed gradient stops into the flexible tail.
effect_path: Gradient stop elements are collected in NSVGgradientData, a shape fill or stroke resolves the referenced gradient, nsvg__createGradient allocates the runtime gradient one stop short, and memcpy copies the full stop list into grad->stops.
guard_p1: A referenced linear or radial gradient has at least two parsed stop elements.
guard_p2: A single-stop gradient fits the embedded stop, and the original nstops - 1 formula allocates exactly the copied stop count.
hardness_reason: The allocation is reached only after defs parsing, gradient reference resolution, object/user-space transform setup, and paint construction.
naturalness_reason: Flexible-array structs commonly use sizeof(base) plus element count minus one; an off-by-one in the extra-element term is a realistic allocation bug.
explanation: The copy count remains nstops. Allocating only nstops - 1 total stop slots makes the final stop overwrite past the gradient object.

edit_summary: Leave the parser path list reachable after transferring it into a returned image shape.
root_cause: nsvg__addShape transfers p->plist into shape->paths, but the parser-side owner must be detached before parser teardown runs.
effect_path: nsvgParse returns p->image after clearing p->image, then nsvg__deleteParser frees p->plist; later the API caller destroys the returned image and nsvgDelete frees the same shape->paths list.
guard_p1: An SVG element creates at least one valid path so nsvg__addShape transfers a non-empty p->plist to shape->paths.
guard_p2: The caller follows the normal parse-then-destroy lifecycle and calls nsvgDelete on the returned image.
hardness_reason: The first free occurs in parser cleanup after the image handoff, while the second free occurs in the public image destructor across a separate API lifecycle phase.
naturalness_reason: Missing a detach after an ownership transfer from parser scratch state into the returned object is a realistic temporal bug in single-header parsers.
explanation: The path list has two owners if p->plist is not cleared after assigning shape->paths. Parser cleanup and image cleanup then traverse and free the same linked list.
first_free_site_expected: nsvg__deleteParser -> nsvg__deletePaths(p->plist) after nsvgParse detaches p->image
second_free_site_expected: nsvgDelete -> nsvg__deletePaths(shape->paths) on the returned image
conditional_expected: Positive SVG has a parsed shape/path and caller destroys the returned image; negative empty/no-path SVG leaves p->plist NULL and avoids the duplicate ownership.

edit_summary: Accept path point counts whose final cubic segment lacks a complete three-point tail.
root_cause: NanoSVG represents paths as one initial point plus groups of three cubic Bezier points, and nsvg__addPath must reject every point count that is not 1 modulo 3.
effect_path: Path commands accumulate points in p->pts, the weakened topology guard accepts a 0-mod-3 count, nsvg__addPath copies that count into path->pts, and the bounds loop calls nsvg__curveBounds on a final curve slice that reads past the point array.
guard_p1: An SVG path command sequence leaves p->npts at 6, 9, or another 0-mod-3 count before path finalization.
guard_p2: A valid 1-mod-3 cubic path remains accepted, while a 2-mod-3 malformed path is still rejected by the injected condition.
hardness_reason: The read occurs after path command parsing, optional close handling, path object allocation/copy, and the later cubic bounds pass.
naturalness_reason: A modulo topology check near path finalization is easy to weaken incorrectly when trying to distinguish malformed tails.
explanation: The original guard rejects both incomplete modulo classes. The injected condition lets 0-mod-3 paths through, so the bounds walker treats an incomplete tail as a full cubic segment.
boundary_invariant: A NanoSVG path must contain 1 + 3*N points before cubic bounds are computed.
boundary_case: A malformed path with six accumulated points reaches nsvg__addPath.
neighbor_case: A valid seven-point path, or the original != 1 guard, keeps every curveBounds slice complete.
oob_site_expected: src/nanosvg.h:1077 reads curve[6] and curve[7] through nsvg__curveBounds for an incomplete final segment.

edit_summary: Miss a one-point growth of the reusable dashed-stroke duplicate buffer.
root_cause: The rasterizer reuses points2 across paths and must grow it whenever the current flattened point count exceeds the previous capacity.
effect_path: A dashed stroked path is flattened into r->points, nsvg__duplicatePoints reuses points2 when the new path is exactly one point larger than the old capacity, and memcpy copies the full point sequence past the stale allocation.
guard_p1: The same rasterizer processes a dashed stroke path whose flattened point count is exactly cpoints2 + 1 after an earlier smaller dashed path established cpoints2.
guard_p2: A path with no point-count growth, or growth by more than one, does not hit the missed exact case under the injected condition.
hardness_reason: The overflow depends on persistent rasterizer capacity state across paths, flattening output, and the dashed-stroke duplicate phase.
naturalness_reason: Reusable scratch buffers often grow only on demand; adding a small slack term to the capacity comparison is a plausible but unsafe optimization.
explanation: The original comparison grows points2 for any larger point count. The injected comparison skips the exact one-point growth case and then memcpy writes one NSVGpoint beyond the old buffer.
boundary_invariant: points2 capacity must be at least r->npoints before copying sizeof(NSVGpoint) * r->npoints bytes.
boundary_case: Two dashed stroked paths on one rasterizer where the later flattened path has exactly one more point than the previous points2 capacity.
neighbor_case: Equal point counts remain in bounds, and growth by two still reallocates under the injected condition.
oob_site_expected: src/nanosvgrast.h:286 copies one NSVGpoint past points2 when r->npoints equals r->cpoints2 + 1.

edit_summary: Miss reallocation when a reused rasterizer grows the scanline width by exactly one pixel.
root_cause: The rasterizer's scanline scratch buffer is cached by width and must be reallocated for any larger target width before memset and coverage fills.
effect_path: A caller reuses an NSVGrasterizer for multiple images, the first rasterization sets cscanline, a later call is exactly one pixel wider, and the injected guard skips realloc before memset clears w bytes in the smaller scanline buffer.
guard_p1: An NSVGrasterizer is reused for a second rasterization whose width is exactly the previous scanline capacity plus one.
guard_p2: The same width reuses the buffer safely, while growth by two still reallocates under the injected guard.
hardness_reason: The memory effect requires cross-call scratch-buffer state in the rasterizer and a later rasterization width boundary, not a malformed SVG token alone.
naturalness_reason: Adding a one-pixel slack assumption to a cached scratch-buffer growth check is a realistic performance-oriented regression.
explanation: The original guard reallocates scanline for every larger width. The injected guard misses exactly one-pixel growth, so the next memset and scanline fill operate past the old allocation.
boundary_invariant: r->scanline must have at least w bytes before nsvg__rasterizeSortedEdges clears and fills coverage for the current output width.
boundary_case: Reuse one rasterizer for widths N and then N + 1.
neighbor_case: Reuse at width N or grow directly to N + 2, which reallocates under the injected guard.
oob_site_expected: src/nanosvgrast.h:1133 clears r->width bytes through r->scanline after nsvgRasterize skipped the one-pixel growth realloc.

edit_summary: Store a ninth stroke dash length into an eight-entry parser attribute array.
root_cause: The parser attribute stores at most NSVG_MAX_DASHES dash lengths before nsvg__addShape copies them into the fixed NSVGshape dash array.
effect_path: Style parsing reaches stroke-dasharray, nsvg__parseStrokeDashArray accepts one extra dash item, the ninth parsed coordinate is stored past attr->strokeDashArray, and shape construction later trusts attr->strokeDashCount while copying dash data for rasterization.
guard_p1: A visible stroked shape has a stroke-dasharray with nine positive dash values.
guard_p2: Eight dash values fit the fixed array, and the original strict bound ignores additional dash items.
hardness_reason: The corrupted parser attribute crosses CSS-style parsing and shape construction before the dash state is consumed by the stroke rasterizer.
naturalness_reason: Dash arrays have a visible fixed maximum and a parser count, making an inclusive maximum check a plausible boundary regression.
explanation: NSVG_MAX_DASHES is the number of valid entries, not the highest valid index. Allowing count == NSVG_MAX_DASHES writes the ninth value one slot past the array.
boundary_invariant: strokeDashArray has indexes 0 through NSVG_MAX_DASHES - 1, and count must stay strictly below the maximum before storing.
boundary_case: A stroke-dasharray style containing nine nonzero lengths.
neighbor_case: Eight nonzero dash lengths or the original strict comparison stays within the array.
oob_site_expected: src/nanosvg.h:1798 writes strokeDashArray[count] with count equal to NSVG_MAX_DASHES.

edit_summary: Allow one more XML attribute pair than the fixed callback vector can hold with its two terminators.
root_cause: The fixed attr vector stores name/value pairs and then appends two NULL terminators before invoking the element callback.
effect_path: The XML tokenizer splits a start tag into attribute pairs, the injected loop admits the pair that occupies the last two vector slots, and the required two terminators are then written beyond attr before nsvg__startElement consumes the list.
guard_p1: An SVG start tag has enough well-formed attributes to fill attr[254] and attr[255] with a final name/value pair.
guard_p2: One fewer attribute pair leaves room for both terminators, and the original -3 bound stops before the vector is full.
hardness_reason: The overflow depends on XML attribute tokenization, pair accounting, and callback-list termination rather than a direct caller-supplied index.
naturalness_reason: Fixed name/value vectors with sentinel terminators often have off-by-one capacity mistakes near the pair limit.
explanation: The parser must reserve two attr entries for NULL terminators. The injected bound fills those entries with an attribute pair, so the terminators overflow the stack array.
boundary_invariant: attr must contain an even number of name/value entries plus two trailing NULL entries within NSVG_XML_MAX_ATTRIBS.
boundary_case: A start element with 128 well-formed attributes reaches the final pair and then appends terminators.
neighbor_case: A start element with 127 attributes or the original -3 bound keeps both terminators in bounds.
oob_site_expected: src/nanosvg.h:326 writes attr[nattr++] after nattr has already reached NSVG_XML_MAX_ATTRIBS.
